A PRIOR CYCLE RECORDED A VERIFICATION THAT WAS FALSE. The 1.0.5 log says 'Verified current (no change, all IDs resolve): ... HeQ mirrors (Etelis + pig4431)'. pig4431/HeQ_v1 returns 404 and was the PRIMARY recommendation in the Step 5 pairing table, a gotcha, dataset-catalog.md and find_dataset.py. Never trust a previous cycle's blanket 'all IDs resolve'; re-run the check. The cheap way is to grep every `org/name` token out of all files and hit the HF API for each, which takes under a minute for 54 ids.

THE LICENCE LAYER WAS WRONG IN THE PERMISSIVE DIRECTION, which is the only direction that costs a user money. HebArabNlpProject was described as 'generally CC-BY-4.0, commercial-friendly' when the API says license: other with no name, and two datasets declare nothing at all. The skill's own references/license-quick-guide.md already said HebrewSentiment 'currently reads other', so the body contradicted its own reference file. Check the body against the reference files, not just against the world.

STATE THE DEFAULT RULE, NOT JUST THE FACTS. The skill listed licences but never said what an ABSENT licence means. It now says: no declared licence is not permission, treat it as all rights reserved and ask the depositor. That single sentence is worth more than any individual licence row because it generalises to datasets added after this cycle.

GATING IS A LICENCE EVENT, NOT A DOWNLOAD DETAIL. Every ivrit.ai dataset is gated=auto while the models are not, so a pipeline fails halfway with a 401 after the model has already downloaded, and acceptance is per HuggingFace account so a laptop can work while a shared training account fails. Clicking Agree is also the act that binds you to the bespoke licence. Record `gated` as a first-class field anywhere licences are recorded.

TWO REVIEWER CLAIMS DID NOT SURVIVE THE PRIMARY SOURCE, both in the direction of deleting or rewriting correct content: the reviewer said `dicta-il/dictabert-char-spacefix` was a phantom id (it returns 200; the real defect was that it was missing from model-catalog.md), and that the Knesset dataset was misattributed to ivrit.ai (ivrit-ai/knesset-plenums genuinely exists; the real finding was that a SECOND, academic, differently-licensed Knesset corpus exists at HaifaCLGroup/KnessetCorpus). Same lesson as the vehicle skill: a reviewer claim is a lead, not a fact.

arXiv's export API returned zero entries for every id including a known-good control, so it was failing rather than the ids being wrong. https://arxiv.org/abs/<id> worked. When a lookup returns nothing, test the lookup with a control before concluding the item does not exist.

[CARRY] NOT DONE, deliberately: the Israeli Ministry of Justice opinion of Dec 2022 on using copyrighted works for machine learning (fair use under s.19 of the Copyright Act 5768-2007), and Privacy Protection Law Amendment 13 obligations on scraped Hebrew text containing personal data. The reviewer is right that these are the two Israeli legal facts that actually govern an Israeli team training on scraped Hebrew, and that a licensing skill for an Israeli audience should carry them. The WebSearch budget was exhausted this cycle and they could not be sourced, and an unverified legal claim in a licensing skill is the highest-cost possible error. Source them first thing next cycle.

[CARRY] The three catalogs (SKILL.md tables, references/*.md, and CATALOG in find_dataset.py) are independent copies and have already drifted on the HeQ id, the hour count and licence posture. Regenerate all three from one shared JSON with `gated` and `license_declared` as first-class fields.

[CARRY] No coverage of how to actually RUN a Hebrew evaluation (lm-evaluation-harness, the Open Hebrew LLM Leaderboard task configs, and the fact that the standard SQuAD normalizer is English-specific and mis-scores Hebrew F1). The skill lists which benchmarks are missing and never says how to run the ones that exist.

A previous em-dash strip replaced every em-dash with ' ,  ' (space-comma-double-space) in SKILL.md only, leaving 49 floating commas; SKILL_HE.md had been cleaned properly. When applying a house-style rule mechanically, check the replacement reads correctly and apply it to both language files.

I MADE THE SAME MIRROR-SWEEP MISTAKE TWICE IN ONE SESSION. On the previous skill the fix landed in the body and the retracted claim survived in references/. Here the licence correction landed in SKILL.md and SKILL_HE.md and the three reference files plus the script kept the pre-correction posture, so a reader consulting the file the skill explicitly points them at (references/license-quick-guide.md, references/model-catalog.md, references/dataset-catalog.md) got the old, wrong answer. Run the grep-to-zero across ALL surfaces BEFORE dispatching the reviewer, not after it comes back. The reviewer should be confirming a sweep already done, not performing it.

A UNIVERSAL QUANTIFIER GENERALISED FROM ONE SAMPLE IS A FABRICATION. I wrote 'every ivrit.ai dataset is gated' after checking a single card. Four of the 28 are not, and one of those four was described as ungated twelve lines earlier in the same file, so the document contradicted itself. When a claim has the shape 'all X are Y', enumerate X. The HF org listing endpoint does this in one call.

THE HF ORG LIST ENDPOINT OMITS cardData. https://huggingface.co/api/models?author=<org> returns records with no license field at all, so every model looks unlicensed. Per-id calls are the only reliable licence check; the list endpoint is reliable for `gated` and for enumeration.

A correction can be right in the body and stale in the gotcha. The OSCAR 'suspended' claim was fixed in Step 2 and survived in the English Gotchas, while the HEBREW gotcha had been fixed. Divergence ran the opposite way from the usual risk. Grep the retracted STRING, not the section.

THE GENERATOR, named once so it stops being rediscovered: A CLAIM ASSERTED ACROSS A SET FROM A SINGLE OBSERVATION. Three instances this cycle, all mine, all the same shape: 'every ivrit.ai dataset is gated' from one card (data); a blanket 'CITED URL IS DEAD, browser-verified' source_note across five URLs after checking four (evidence, on the previous skill); and one hardcoded --commercial exclusion reason applied to every entry (code), which told the reader that a cc-by-4.0 dataset had an undeclared licence. The counter-discipline is to enumerate one at a time and never sample and generalise.

THE DURABLE FIX FOR THAT GENERATOR IS STRUCTURAL, NOT VERBAL. Rewording a sentence to be true of more cases still leaves it hardcoded. Deriving it from the entry means it CANNOT contradict the data it describes. `--verify-licences` goes one step further and turns the whole class into a test: for every single-slash id, fetch the card and assert the licence matches. Fifteen lines, and it caught five apparent mismatches on its first run which were actually a flaw in my comparison (license: other is only meaningful together with license_name), so the check improved the checker too.

A DEVELOPER CHECK MUST DISTINGUISH 'FAILED' FROM 'COULD NOT RUN'. The first version used urllib and reported all 13 entries as mismatched, because this machine's Python has no CA bundle. That is indistinguishable from a real failure unless you look. It now shells out to curl and reports UNREACHABLE separately, and fails on either, because a check that could not run has not passed. Same principle as treating a gov.il 403 as unverified rather than as bot-blocked.
